Use the Wayback Machine to capture Ben & Jerry’s online Flavor Graveyard as it existed at the end of 2022. Objectives: (1) Identify all flavors listed in the Flavor Graveyard as of December 2022, (2) for each flavor, record the introduction year and retirement year as printed on the headstone (e.g., YYYY–YYYY) or otherwise stated on the flavor’s page, (3) record the archived URL of the flavor’s page and the hero/headstone image URL, and (4) determine which flavor(s) qualify as the “oldest” under multiple plausible definitions: (a) earliest introduction year (release year), (b) earliest retirement year, and (c) earliest-listed entry on the graveyard page if a chronological order is presented. Also note any official language on the site (archived) that defines or references the "oldest" flavor. \n\nScope & method:\n- Start with archived snapshots of https://www.benjerry.com/flavors/flavor-graveyard (or equivalent URL) in December 2022. Prefer 31 Dec 2022; if image/content missing, try nearby late-December snapshots. If the site structure differs, find the correct graveyard index page. \n- Enumerate every flavor shown in the graveyard directory at that time. If the directory only links to individual pages where dates are provided, open each linked flavor page (archived December 2022) to extract the headstone’s date range (e.g., 1986–1991). \n- For each flavor entry, output: flavor name; intro year; retirement year; archived URL of flavor page; archived URL of the headstone/hero image used on the flavor page (prefer highest resolution); and any notable details (e.g., release/retirement years missing or contradictory). If multiple snapshots differ slightly, prefer the latest December 2022 snapshot that renders images and text correctly, but note differences.\n- Produce a ranked list of “oldest” candidates under each definition above (earliest intro year; earliest retirement year; earliest listing if the page order is chronological). If multiple flavors share the earliest year, list them all. \n- Provide direct archive URLs for the index page(s), for each flavor page, and for each image used. \n- Deliver results in a structured summary (list or table) plus a brief narrative on methodology and any uncertainties encountered.

Analyze the archived Dastardly Mash flavor page hero image (as of end of 2022) to extract the last line of the rhyme from a background headstone visible in that photo.

Scope & method:
1) Retrieve the Dastardly Mash flavor page from the Wayback Machine in late December 2022 if available; otherwise use the closest early-2023 capture that still reflects late-2022 content. Candidate URLs already found:
- http://web.archive.org/web/20230129142151/https://www.benjerry.com/flavors/flavor-graveyard/dastardly-mash
If a December 2022 capture exists, prefer it; otherwise use the above.
2) On the archived page, identify the hero/headstone image (often located under files/live/sites/systemsite/files/flavors/flavor-graveyard/detail-images/dastardly-mash-detail.png). Download/view the full-resolution archived image (use the "im_" Wayback URL variant if needed) and zoom in.
3) Inspect the photo to identify any background headstone that is at least partially readable. Determine the flavor name on that background headstone and transcribe the rhyme text visible under the flavor name. Focus on the last line of the rhyme (the line directly above the dates), including punctuation and capitalization.
4) If the background rhyme text is partially obscured or not fully legible, identify the background flavor by its name on the stone, then open that flavor’s own archived flavor-page (Dec 2022 preferred; nearest available otherwise) to confirm the exact rhyme wording. Capture the precise last line as of end-of-2022.
5) Provide:
- The archive URL of the Dastardly Mash page used and the direct archived URL of the hero image file analyzed.
- A short description of the background headstone selected (flavor name, position in image) and the full rhyme as transcribed from the image if readable; otherwise, the confirmed last line from that flavor’s page.
- The exact last line of the background headstone’s rhyme, quoted exactly with punctuation/capitalization.
- Any uncertainties (e.g., multiple background stones visible with different rhymes, image changes across snapshots) and screenshots/crops if helpful.
